worked_example.title: Compare greedy choice and sequence probability

blocks.text: Greedy decoding chooses the largest next-token probability at each step, with an explicit tie rule if needed. It does not always maximise the probability of a complete sequence. Counterexample: first-step A=0.6 and B=0.4. Given A, end=0.51 and x=0.49; given B, end=1. Greedy produces A,end with probability 0.306. The path B,end has probability 0.4, larger than 0.306. This comparison concerns exactly two-step paths; longer completion probabilities require the later conditionals too.
A high path probability measures the model’s preference over these specified paths. It is not evidence that a status claim matches a live observation. Format checks and source checks remain separate.

independent_case.title: Analyse a new table independently
independent_case.task: First tokens go=0.4, wait=0.35, ask=0.25. End probabilities given them are 0.5,0.8,1 respectively; each branch has a complementary more token. Compute all three end-path probabilities and their sum. Which first token is greedy, which end path is largest, and does either verify a real status?
independent_case.answer: Teacher explanation: End-path probabilities 0.2,0.28,0.25; sum 0.73. Greedy first token is go, but wait,end is the largest of the specified end paths. Neither establishes a real status without appropriate evidence.

blocks.text: A closer explanation

The probability of ready followed by end is 0.5*0.8 = 0.4. Ready followed by today is 0.5*0.2 = 0.1. Busy followed by end is 0.3*0.5 = 0.15, and busy followed by today is 0.15. Unknown followed by end is 0.2 and unknown followed by today is 0. Together these six two-step paths sum to 1. These products are chain-rule calculations; they do not assume the second token is independent of the first.

The same red token now has [1,0] at position 0 and [3,0] at position 1. Both token identity and position affect the represented row. Addition requires equal widths; adding a three-component position vector to a two-component embedding violates the input contract. Record the position numbering and embedding-table version.
